pages.running_header: שַׁחֲרִית לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה

blocks.text: יִשְׁעֵנוּ: לְדוֹר וָדוֹר הוּא קַיָּם וּשְׁמוֹ קַיָּם וְכִסְאוֹ נָכוֹן וּמַלְכוּתוֹ וֶאֱמוּנָתוֹ לָעַד קַיֶּמֶת: וּדְבָרָיו חָיִים וְקַיָּמִים נֶאֱמָנִים וְנֶחֱמָדִים לָעַד וּלְעוֹלְמֵי עוֹלָמִים עַל־אֲבוֹתֵינוּ וְעָלֵינוּ עַל־בָּנֵינוּ וְעַל־דּוֹרוֹתֵינוּ וְעַל כָּל־דּוֹרוֹת זֶרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבָדֶיךָ:
uncertainties: יִשְׁעֵנוּ: there is a dot under the first yod, which I read as a hiriq.
קַיֶּמֶת: I read a segol under the yod (קַיֶּ), not a qamats.
חָיִים: I see no dagesh in the yod.
דּוֹרוֹתֵינוּ (after וְעַל־): I cannot confirm the dagesh in the dalet.
וְעַל כָּל־דּוֹרוֹת: there is a space and no maqaf between וְעַל and כָּל. A small tick on the lamed of וְעַל looks like the top of the letter or a printing mark, not a vowel.
The dagesh in the dalet of כָּל־דּוֹרוֹת is unclear.

blocks.text: עַל־הָרִאשׁוֹנִים וְעַל־הָאַחֲרוֹנִים דָּבָר טוֹב וְקַיָּם לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. אֱמֶת וֶאֱמוּנָה חֹק וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר: אֱמֶת שָׁאַתָּה הוּא יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ. מַלְכֵּנוּ מֶלֶךְ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ גּוֹאֲלֵנוּ גּוֹאֵל אֲבוֹתֵינוּ יוֹצְרֵנוּ צוּר יְשׁוּעָתֵנוּ פּוֹדֵנוּ וּמַצִּילֵנוּ מֵעוֹלָם שְׁמֶךָ. אֵין אֱלֹהִים זוּלָתֶךָ:
uncertainties: וֶאֱמוּנָה: there is a small comma-like mark or dot just after or above the final he. It could be a stray mark or a printed comma. I did not record a mappiq.
שָׁאַתָּה: I read qamats under the shin and patah under the alef, but these are small. Check the patah under the alef.
גּוֹאֲלֵנוּ and גּוֹאֵל: the dagesh in the gimel is faint.
The page has the divine name abbreviation יְיָ, not the Tetragrammaton.

blocks.text: עֶזְרַת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ אַתָּה הוּא מֵעוֹלָם מָגֵן וּמוֹשִׁיעַ לִבְנֵיהֶם אַחֲרֵיהֶם בְּכָל־דּוֹר וָדוֹר: בְּרוּם עוֹלָם מוֹשָׁבֶךָ וּמִשְׁפָּטֶיךָ וְצִדְקָתְךָ עַד־אַפְסֵי אָרֶץ: אַשְׁרֵי אִישׁ שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע לְמִצְוֹתֶיךָ וְתוֹרָתְךָ וּדְבָרְךָ יָשִׂים עַל־לִבּוֹ: אֱמֶת אַתָּה הוּא אָדוֹן לְעַמֶּךָ וּמֶלֶךְ גִּבּוֹר לָרִיב רִיבָם: אֱמֶת אַתָּה הוּא רִאשׁוֹן וְאַתָּה הוּא אַחֲרוֹן וּמִבַּלְעָדֶיךָ אֵין לָנוּ מֶלֶךְ גּוֹאֵל וּמוֹשִׁיעַ: מִמִּצְרַיִם גְּאַלְתָּנוּ יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וּמִבֵּית עֲבָדִים פְּדִיתָנוּ. כָּל־בְּכוֹרֵיהֶם הָרַגְתָּ וּבְכוֹרְךָ גָּאָלְתָּ וְיַם־סוּף בָּקַעְתָּ וְזֵדִים טִבַּעְתָּ וִידִידִים הֶעֱבַרְתָּ וַיְכַסּוּ מַיִם צָרֵיהֶם אֶחָד מֵהֶם לֹא נוֹתָר: עַל־זֹאת שִׁבְּחוּ אֲהוּבִים וְרוֹמְמוּ אֵל וְנָתְנוּ יְדִידִים זְמִירוֹת שִׁירוֹת וְתִשְׁבָּחוֹת בְּרָכוֹת וְהוֹדָאוֹת לְמֶלֶךְ אֵל חַי וְקַיָּם: רָם וְנִשָּׂא גָּדוֹל וְנוֹרָא מַשְׁפִּיל גֵּאִים וּמַגְבִּיהַּ שְׁפָלִים מוֹצִיא אֲסִירִים וּפוֹדֶה עֲנָוִים וְעוֹזֵר דַּלִּים וְעוֹנֶה לְעַמּוֹ בְּעֵת שַׁוְּעָם אֵלָיו: תְּהִלּוֹת לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּמְבֹרָךְ. מֹשֶׁה וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְךָ עָנוּ שִׁירָה בְּשִׂמְחָה רַבָּה וְאָמְרוּ כֻלָּם:
uncertainties: גּוֹאֵל in מֶלֶךְ גּוֹאֵל וּמוֹשִׁיעַ (line 7 of this paragraph): the alef is badly printed or broken. Only a small mark with a dot shows between the vav and the lamed, so the consonants could be read as גּוֹל. I kept גּוֹאֵל as the probable reading, and the tsere under the alef is also uncertain. Please check against the physical copy.
לְמִצְוֹתֶיךָ: there is a dot above the vav, which I read as a holam (מִצְוֹ).
עַל־זֹאת: the holam over the zayin or alef is small.
וּמַגְבִּיהַּ: I read a mappiq dot in the final he, with a patah under it.
שַׁוְּעָם: I read a dagesh in the vav plus a shva.

pages.running_header: Morning Prayer for the New Year
pages.continuation_in: The page opens mid-sentence with "to generation does He endure…", continuing from the previous English page (expected to end with "…From generation"). No paragraph indent.
pages.continuation_out: The page ends at "all of them said:" and the text continues on the next English page (the Mi khamokha verse). The lower part of the page is blank.

blocks.text: to generation does He endure and His Name endures, His throne is firmly founded and His realm and His faithfulness endure for ever. And His words are living and eternal, faithful and delightful always and in all eternity for our fathers and for us, for our children and our coming generations and all the generations of the seed of Israel Thy servants.
uncertainties: The source breaks "faith-/ful" across a line. I rejoined it as "faithful".

blocks.text: For the first and the last it is a good and everlasting word, truth and faithfulness, a statute that never passes away. It is truth that Thou, O Lord, art our God and the God of our fathers, our King, the King of our fathers, our Redeemer, the Redeemer of our fathers, our Creator, the Rock of our salvation, our deliverer and rescuer, that is Thy Name since eternity, there is no God except Thee.

The aid of our fathers hast Thou ever been, shield and helper of their children after them in every generation. In the heights of the world is Thy dwelling and Thy judgments and Thy love extend to the ends of the earth. Fortunate the man, who listens to Thy commandments and takes Thy Torah and Thy word to heart. In truth Thou art the Lord for Thy people and a strong King to promote their cause. In truth Thou art the first and Thou art the last and except for Thee we have no King, Redeemer or helper. From Egypt has Thou redeemed us, O Lord our God, and from the house of slaves hast Thou freed us. All their first born hast Thou slain and Thy first born redeemed, divided the Sea of Reeds, drowned the arrogant and led those dear to Thee through to safety. Then the waters covered their enemies, not one of them remained. Thereupon those who were loved, sang and praised God and those dear to Him offered hymns of praise, songs and glorification, blessings and thanks to the King, the living, eternal God. Lofty and exalted, great and awe-inspiring, He lowers the proud, raises the lowly, leads prisoners to freedom, redeems the meek, helps the poor and hears His people at the time when they implore Him. Praiscs to the supreme God, blessed is He and called blessed. Moses and the children of Israel intoned a song to Thee with great rejoicing and all of them said:
uncertainties: "Praiscs" is printed this way, apparently a typo for "Praises". I kept it as printed.
"From Egypt has Thou" is printed this way, not "hast Thou". I kept it as printed.
"awe-inspiring" has a real hyphen in the middle of the line. I kept it.

notes: Scans s114 (Hebrew) and s115 (English) face each other as printed page 43. Each has three paragraphs that line up one to one: the end of Emet veyatziv, Al harishonim, and Ezrat avoteinu (through וְאָמְרוּ כֻלָּם / 'all of them said:').

I did not repeat words where the image bands overlap. The last line of band1 and the first line of band2 (פּוֹדֵנוּ … זוּלָתֶךָ: / 'eternity, there is no God except Thee.') each appear only once. The same applies to the line shared by band2 and band3 (הֶעֱבַרְתָּ … / 'Then the waters covered…').
Neither scan has Rashi-script rubrics, speaker sigla, Biblical citations, or cantillation. The Hebrew has vowel points only, with no te'amim.
Neither scan has bracketed or parenthetical Shabbat alternatives.
The English linkage cues are the Hebrew words על and עזרת, printed at the start of the second and third English paragraphs. They are cues, not prayer text.

Suggested corrections (the printed text above stays literal): s115 'Praiscs' → 'Praises'. s115 'From Egypt has Thou redeemed us' → 'hast Thou' (optional, since this may be the translator's own wording). s114 גּוֹאֵל in מֶלֶךְ גּוֹאֵל וּמוֹשִׁיעַ: the alef is damaged in print, so confirm the consonants.
Paragraph 1 is split at וּמַלְכוּתוֹ / וֶאֱמוּנָתוֹ only by the line break. There is no paragraph break there.
